name: whoami
title: Understanding whoami
summary: whoami displays information about the currently logged-on user and their security context (account name, SID, groups, and privileges) on Windows.

examples.description: Shows the current user in DOMAIN\User or COMPUTERNAME\User format.
Displays the current user as a User Principal Name (UPN), e.g., user@contoso.com (requires domain account).
Displays the user name using the domain's fully qualified domain name (FQDN), e.g., corp.contoso.com\user (requires domain context).
Shows the current user and their Security Identifier (SID).
Lists group memberships and attributes (e.g., Mandatory, Enabled, Deny-only).
Lists security privileges in the current logon token and whether each is enabled or disabled.
Displays comprehensive identity details: user, SID, groups, privileges, and logon information.
Shows the hexadecimal logon session ID (LUID) for the current session.

permissions.notes: whoami reads the current token and does not modify system state. It works for standard users; some fields may vary based on token filtering or service contexts.

risk.warning: Reveals identity and security details to the console; avoid sharing outputs that contain sensitive SIDs or account names.

output_fields.name: /USER
output_fields.description: Reveals the user and SID; useful to confirm which account (and SID) the process is running under.

output_fields.name: /GROUPS -> Attributes
output_fields.description: Indicates group influence on access (e.g., Deny-only, Mandatory, Enabled by default). Critical when troubleshooting permission issues.

output_fields.name: /PRIV -> State
output_fields.description: Shows whether sensitive privileges (e.g., SeBackupPrivilege) are enabled; affects ability to perform certain actions.

output_fields.name: /LOGONID
output_fields.description: Identifies the specific logon session (LUID), helping correlate with security logs or session diagnostics.

output_fields.name: /UPN
output_fields.description: Outputs user@domain format; helpful for SSO/Kerberos troubleshooting in domain environments.

output_fields.name: /FQDN
output_fields.description: Displays the user with the domain’s FQDN; helps avoid ambiguity with NetBIOS names.

common_errors.message: 'whoami' is not recognized as an internal or external command, operable program or batch file.
common_errors.meaning: Occurs if system paths to System32 are missing from PATH, the binary is unavailable, or on very old/stripped environments. Run from %SystemRoot%\System32 or fix PATH.

common_errors.message: ERROR: Invalid syntax. Type "WHOAMI /?" for usage.
common_errors.meaning: Triggered by unsupported or misspelled switches (e.g., /domain). Use whoami /? to see valid options.

common_errors.message: UPN/FQDN not available for this account.
common_errors.meaning: The account is local or the system cannot contact a domain controller. Ensure the user is a domain account and the DC is reachable.

common_errors.message: Insufficient resources to complete the operation.
common_errors.meaning: Rare; indicates a transient system resource issue when querying token details. Retry or check system health.
